correctness.rationale: The proof is correct. For every positive integer N, N divides F_m exactly when z(N) divides m. For an odd prime q not equal to 5, the standard lifting dichotomy gives z(q^2)=z(q) in the Wall--Sun--Sun case and z(q^2)=q z(q) otherwise; also z(q) divides pi(q) and q does not divide pi(q). The progression intersection is therefore empty unless z(q) divides r, and when nonempty has relative density 1 in the exceptional case or 1/q in the ordinary case. On terms with q^2 not dividing F_m, divisibility of phi(F_m) by q must come from a prime divisor p not equal to q with p congruent to 1 modulo q. A fresh direct computation reproduced the rank/period identities for several small primes; the finite script is only a sanity check.
residual_risks: No Wall--Sun--Sun prime is known, so the density-one branch is conditional on existence.
